current_example.problem: Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+9x$ in the interval $[0,2].$ Calculate the first two iterations of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization starting at the point $x_0=0.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f'(x_n)}{f''(x_n)},
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ and $f''(x_n)$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n,$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+9x)^{′}=3{x}^{2}-12x+9, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(3{x}^{2}-12x+9)^{′}=6x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{3{x}_{n}^{2}-12{x}_{n}+9}{6{x}_{n}-12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{3{x}_{0}^{2}-12{x}_{0}+9}{6{x}_{0}-12} \\  & =0-\frac{3(0)^{2}-12(0)+9}{6(0)-12} \\  & =\frac{9}{12} \\  & =0.75\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{3{x}_{1}^{2}-12{x}_{1}+9}{6{x}_{1}-12} \\  & =0.75-\frac{3(0.75)^{2}-12(0.75)+9}{6(0.75)-12} \\  & =0.975\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x_1 = 0.75$ and $x_2 = 0.975.$
